target.problem: An adequacy oracle parsed zero clauses and returned CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS even though the task had a clear four-bullet definition_of_done. The parser read the wrong location and received an empty object/list. Diagnose the failure shape and propose a falsifiable check that distinguishes ambiguous content from failed extraction.

source.label: receipt_defect
source.surface: An empty grep for one target was generalized into a universal claim that no targets existed.

roles.population_wide_absence: absence across the complete search space

source.transferred_lesson: Enumerate the full population and report query scope; seed a known matching item to show the query can return positive.

structural.candidate_text: The contract parser returned zero clauses and labeled the contract ambiguous, but the actual contract content is a clear four-bullet definition of done. The zero result came from reading the wrong location, not from ambiguity. To distinguish ambiguous content from failed extraction, enumerate all possible contract locations and parse each one. If any location yields the four-bullet definition, then the ambiguity claim is falsified. This check directly tests whether the content is truly ambiguous or merely inaccessible.
